item.title: Drummer Marcus Gilmore Creates Continuous Melodies (From the Archives)
item.description: Drummer and composer Marcus Gilmore looks to the creative openness of his drum elders – like his grandfather, Roy Haynes, the late tabla master Zakir Hussain, or renaissance man and drummer Milford Graves - and underscores the drum set as melodic instrument – exploiting all of the potential of the components – bending notes, playing with the natural vibrations, or augmenting his set up with Sunhouse Sensory Percussion. item.title: Marcus Gilmore – "Excerpts of Nube" (Soundcheck Podcast)
item.description: Marcus Gilmore – "Excerpts of Nube" (Soundcheck Podcast) Marcus Gilmore has both the chops and the pedigree to be a top shelf jazz drummer. He’s the grandson of legendary jazz drummer Roy Haynes, and has played with dozens of leading musicians on the scene. But Gilmore is also sonically omnivorous, as likely to play with an Indian tabla master or a rapper as he is with a piano trio. item.title: Louie Vega and Elements of LIfe at Blue Note
item.description: Louie Vega and The Elements of Life With Special Guests at Blue NoteFeb. 19-22. 8PM and 10:30PM. $60.76-$77.65 Louie Vega has been a fixture on the New York dance scene since the 1980s. item.title: Say She She at WARSAW
item.description: Say She She at WARSAWFeb. 20. 7PM. $37.50+up The three singers who lead the group Say She She are all classically trained, but they all like different things: 70s style New York dance music, classic soul and R&B, the swirling psychedelia of Turkish pop or Hindi film music. Together they make a kind of post-disco pop that features an effortless but irresistible dance beat and the trio’s own rich and subtle vocal harmonies.
